A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EG-CFG research, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained, relocated, and newly added material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DeepSeek benchmark evaluations, runtime measurements, component ablations, and a manual analysis of MBPP failures.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds DS-1000 results, additional baseline evaluations, and experiments increasing baseline retry budgets.

M1.justification: The execution-guided CFG pipeline is retained. v1 Section 3.3 describes progressively increasing guidance strength within each configuration, whereas v2 Section 3.4 and Algorithm 1 assign it within each parallel agent's configuration. Because v1 already describes full parallelization and first-success termination elsewhere, it is unclear whether scheduling changed or an inconsistent description was clarified.

E1.justification: v2 adds DS-1000, extending evaluation to 1,000 data-science tasks involving libraries such as Pandas and NumPy. This introduces a distinct domain beyond the retained general Python and competitive-programming benchmarks.

E2.justification: Comparisons expand across several experiments: HumanEval Table 2 adds LDB/LLaMA 3 and QualityFlow/Claude-Sonnet-3.5; CodeContests Table 3 adds CodeSim evaluated with DeepSeek-V3. New DS-1000 Table 4 includes CONLINE, SelfEvolve, DocPrompting, and additional model baselines. Methods already appearing elsewhere in v1 are counted only for their newly added comparison settings.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an MBPP budget-control experiment increasing MGDebugger and MapCoder retries from 5 to 200, plus DS-1000 evaluation using a single input-output example and hidden tests. It also describes the minimal-trace ablation as the final trace event rather than only final variable values and types. Existing models, hyperparameter grids, and accuracy metrics remain; newly disclosed hidden-test use on retained benchmarks does not establish changed splits.

E4.justification: v2 adds retry-budget sensitivity analysis testing whether substantially more baseline attempts close the MBPP performance gap. It removes v1's manual review of 17 unsolved MBPP tasks, including the finding that nine had invalid tests. The original beam-search, CFG, and trace ablation scores remain unchanged in renumbered Table 6.

E5.justification: Both versions report identical per-task runtime means and standard deviations in v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 5. Neither introduces accuracy confidence intervals, seed information, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. Increased search retries are computational budgets, not statistical replications.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 revise EG-CFG/DeepSeek-V3 accuracy from 96.95% to 99.4% on HumanEval, 87.19% to 89.02% on HumanEval-ET, and 58.18% to 60.6% on CodeContests, with corresponding RSR changes. New results include DS-1000 accuracy of 69.9% versus the 38.9% DeepSeek baseline, CodeSim's 52.72% on CodeContests, and 200-retry MBPP scores of 93.6% for MGDebugger and 88.8% for MapCoder. Original MBPP, runtime, and component-ablation values remain unchanged. The cause of the revised existing EG-CFG scores is not explained.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 10 adds an explicit definition of traces as sequences of six-field runtime-event tuples, with event types restricted to call, line, return, and exception. The minimal trace is then defined through the final event. The correctness condition and CFG interpolation remain unchanged; no theorems, proofs, or guarantees are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the performance claims to data science through DS-1000. HumanEval changes from competitive performance below LPW to matching LDB's reported state of the art. The principal contributions concerning incremental execution feedback, CFG, and parallelism remain.

C2.justification: v2 newly argues that wall-clock time is the fairest comparison because of parallelism and interprets the increased-retry experiment as showing that feedback quality, rather than compute quantity, explains the advantage. The benchmark-error explanation for nine MBPP failures is removed. Limitations concerning computational overhead, test availability, and missing task decomposition are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix C supplies controller and inference-loop pseudocode. The method description specifies a custom debugger, runtime-event fields, prefix construction, and newline-based candidate stopping; Section 4 explicitly documents hidden-test separation. The relocated prompt example also corrects the expected output for 'aabc' from 'c' to 'b'. These substantially expand operational documentation, while hardware, model endpoints, hyperparameter grids, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for DS-1000, SelfEvolve, CONLINE, and DocPrompting, extending positioning toward data-science code generation. The APPS reference is replaced by MMLU. The additional preprint citation for Stay on Topic with Classifier-Free Guidance matches a work already cited in published form. The broader positioning against sequential refinement remains stable.

P1.justification: The six main sections remain, with localized rewrites of method and experimental descriptions, compressed baseline and results prose, and correction of 'Context-Free' to 'Classifier-Free'. v2 introduces Section 3.4, relocates the dynamic-prompt explanation to Appendix B, and adds Appendix C. Most of the surrounding narrative is retained.

P2.justification: Overview charts are redrawn with more compact proportions and labels; the HumanEval figure also redisplays previously tabulated MGDebugger results. v2 adds DS-1000 Figure 3 and Table 4, two algorithm panels, and expanded comparison tables. The former Figure 4 moves to Appendix B as Figure 7 and is substantially redesigned with separated, shaded code and trace blocks.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through a distinct data-science benchmark and broader comparisons, makes hidden-test use explicit, and improves reproducibility through Appendix C. These benefits outweigh the removed MBPP failure analysis, but the gain is limited: the retry experiment does not establish matched total computational cost, while its interpretation claims to isolate feedback quality from compute.
